Note: the verifier doesn't distinguish border rows vs interior — it treats any run of length 1 as a seed, any run of length >=2 as a palette. So to be safe, I should construct grids where palettes are only on top/bottom rows and anchors are single cells in interior.

Wait, but the verifier treats ALL length-1 runs as seeds, including on border rows. In the example, top row has a palette 9,2,1. Bottom row has palette 7,5,4 and 6,1,8. Seeds: (1,1,4), (3,2,9), (5,10,7), (7,5,8). Note (1,1,4)→ palette 7,5,4 contains 4 at index 2, start_c = 1-2 = -1, place at columns -1..1, so column 0 gets 5 (j=1), column 1 gets 4 (j=2). Output row1: [5,4,...]. Yes.

Anchor 9 at (3,2): palette 9,2,1, index 0, start 2, place 9,2,1 at cols 2,3,4. Output matches.

Anchor 7 at (5,10): palette 7,5,4 index 0 → place at 10,11,12: 7,5,4. Matches.

Anchor 8 at (7,5): palette 6,1,8 index 2 → start 5-2=3, cols 3,4,5: 6,1,8. Matches.

Careful: palette groups must be distinct colors within a group (per rule). Also seed logic: any length-1 run becomes seed. If a palette is on border row and there's also a single non-black cell in interior, fine.

Let me also avoid a placed group overlapping another anchor? The verifier doesn't care; it just writes. But rule says no palette group overlaps another when placed. I'll keep it clean.
